identity_contract.authentication_user: Revocable login identity. Current access requires live workspace roles and exact audience-purpose grants.
identity_contract.subject_principal: Stable identity of the person whose Brain this is. Auth-user removal cannot erase it.
identity_contract.operator_principal_and_custody: Stable operator identity plus customer-authorised, workspace-scoped custody history. Transfer does not grant access.
identity_contract.historical_principal: Immutable legacy identity retained for authority-fingerprint and ciphertext compatibility. It never grants access or current custody.

behavioral_proof.operator_identity_separation: Operator principals use independent UUIDs and auth links rather than reusing auth-user IDs.
behavioral_proof.planned_transfer_then_removal: Two differently-subjected workspaces, including a dual-role subject, remain intact after both custody assignments transfer and the former auth user is removed.
behavioral_proof.access_revocation: Former auth links, roles and grants are absent; an outstanding JWT reads zero receipts.
behavioral_proof.replacement_access: Replacement custody alone sees no data; explicit roles and grants make exactly one prepared receipt visible.
behavioral_proof.out_of_band_removal: Brain data survives and custody becomes transfer_required until an authorised recovery transfer completes.
behavioral_proof.history_preservation: Ciphertext, authority fingerprint and historical owner UUID remain byte-identical.
behavioral_proof.concurrency_guards: A unique partial index permits one current custody assignment and the transfer function locks the workspace custody row.
behavioral_proof.crypto_compatibility: Original prepared ciphertext decrypts after current custody changes; rewriting historical owner changes the authority fingerprint and fails authenticated decryption.

negative_controls: historical owner rebound to auth.users RESTRICT
stable subject rebound to auth.users CASCADE
historical owner rewrite during cryptographic read
residuals: Current prepared-write functions still use the legacy owner_id name and are not runtime-bound to stable custody.
Customer closure is represented but not exercised.
Anti-revival tombstone purpose, duration, expiry and re-consent remain unresolved.
Multi-connection transfer races, Supabase-local image and PostgREST parity remain untested.
Non-FK identifiers, storage, external processors and provider receipts remain outside this proof.
next_gate: Bind new prepared writes and the principal-removal planner to stable custody without changing historical receipt bytes, then resolve anti-revival tombstone retention before proposing a migration.
